newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bullish German shares hit fresh records.
newsitem.headline: Bullish German shares hit fresh records.

text.p: German shares advanced after a slow start on Thursday, with the DAX led up by the futures market to fresh record highs and coming tantalisingly close to the magical 3,000-point level.
Dealers, who have been aiming for days to push the DAX over the key 3,000 threshold, said the rally was not over yet.
"The champagne bottles will be out," said a Frankfurt trader. "There is more in this market. The uptrend is definitely still there."

The DAX closed the bourse session up 4.86 points at a record closing high of 2,993.31, having earlier hit a record intra-day high of 2,998.61 and having risen over 20 points from an early low of 2,970.45.
In post-bourse trade, a strong performance on Wall Street helped push the IBIS DAX index even higher to end at 2,996.12, up 19.56 points on the day.
The market was weakened slightly at the start after an overnight drop on Wall Street but proved resilient enough to track the futures market into positive territory.

March DTB DAX futures, which have been volatile ahead of an options expiry deadline tomorrow, galavanised the cash market into action by vaulting the 3,000 point level. They were ended up 21.5 points at 3,011.5.
Dealers noted a sharp shift in sector preferences, with bank shares now firmly in demand, replacing the clear favourites of recent weeks -- chemical stocks.
Deutsche Bank rose 1.67 marks to 78.47 marks in bourse trade and ended IBIS at 78.55, while Dresdner Bank rose 65 pfennigs to 51.15 marks in bourse, later edging up to 51.30.
Dealers said bank shares had not kept up with chemical stocks' recent rally and were now starting to make up lost ground.

At the same time, BASF AG slipped 99 pfennigs to 59.60 marks in bourse trade, before paring its loss to end at 59.75 marks while Hoechst AG slipped to 87 pfennigs to 69.58 marks in floor trade before ending IBIS at 69.70.

Utility RWE jumped to as high as 70 marks in bourse trade before settling back to 68.80 marks, up 40 pfennigs, after news that it was to receive partial damages for delays in operating a nuclear power plant. It ended IBIS trade at 68.70 marks.
For the DAX as a whole, the 3,000 point level has no technical significance, but is rather seen as a key psycological boost for the market.
"It will certainly look better on paper," was one trader's comment. "But it will not mean a brand new era."
